question.title: Identifying Consecutive Logs
question.desc: You have a table of user login logs with user IDs and login times. Find all user IDs that have logged in for three consecutive days.
question.setup: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS login_logs; CREATE TABLE login_logs (user_id INT, login_time DATE); INSERT INTO login_logs (user_id, login_time) VALUES (1, '2022-01-01'), (1, '2022-01-02'), (1, '2022-01-03'), (2, '2022-01-01'), (2, '2022-01-03'), (3, '2022-01-01'), (3, '2022-01-02'), (3, '2022-01-03');
question.solution: WITH consecutive_logs AS ( SELECT user_id, login_time, login_time - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY login_time) AS diff FROM login_logs ) SELECT DISTINCT user_id FROM consecutive_logs WHERE login_time - (SELECT MIN(login_time) FROM consecutive_logs cl2 WHERE cl2.user_id = consecutive_logs.user_id) = 2
question.tips: Consider using window functions to identify consecutive sequences.
hints: Use window functions to assign a row number to each login for a user, ordered by time.
Calculate the difference between the login time and the row number for each user.
Filter the results to find users with three consecutive logins.
